# Firmware-provider comparison — who ships what, honestly

*Generated by [`scripts/provider-comparison.py`](scripts/provider-comparison.py) from **live probes** of
real artifacts (Richard Hughes' python-uswid Dell/Lenovo coSWID examples, this repo's own OVMF
CycloneDX SBOM, and prebuilt OVMF / coreboot / Intel blobs on external storage). Last run: 2026-08-08.*

This is the answer to "map real firmware providers to their supply-chain-transparency state and rate
them." Nothing here is asserted — each cell is a probe of a real artifact, and a dimension a probe
cannot evaluate (artifact unmounted, format unreadable) is **UNKNOWN (❔)**, never a pass. As expected,
**no provider satisfies every dimension**, and most of the ecosystem ships **no SBOM at all** — that RED
is the truthful, useful finding, consistent with "&lt;1% of LVFS firmware ships an SBOM."

## Rating matrix

| Provider | SBOM | Format | Embedded | Identity | Source-hash | Byte-hash | Signed | Reconcile | Score |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| **This project — OVMF + `-Y SBOM`** | ✅ | cyclonedx | ⛔ | ✅ | ⛔ | ◐ | ✅ | ✅ | **4.5** |
| **Dell** (XPS13, via uswid) | ✅ | coswid | ✅ | ✅ | ◐ | ❔ | ❔ | ⛔ | **3.5** |
| **Lenovo** (X1 Carbon, via uswid) | ✅ | coswid | ✅ | ✅ | ◐ | ❔ | ❔ | ⛔ | **3.5** |
| Ubuntu OVMF prebuilt (`.deb`) | ⛔ | none | ⛔ | ⛔ | ⛔ | ⛔ | ⛔ | ⛔ | 0.0 |
| coreboot (blobs) | ⛔ | none | ⛔ | ⛔ | ⛔ | ⛔ | ⛔ | ⛔ | 0.0 |
| Intel FSP / microcode | ⛔ | none | ⛔ | ⛔ | ⛔ | ⛔ | ⛔ | ⛔ | 0.0 |

*✅ yes · ◐ partial (some components) · ⛔ no · ❔ unknown (not probed). Score = count of met dimensions
(yes=1, partial=0.5), excluding Format. Regenerate: `make provider-comparison`.*

## Dimensions

| Column | What it means | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| **SBOM** | ships any SBOM/coSWID at all | you cannot verify a bill of materials you do not have |
| **Format** | coswid / cyclonedx / spdx / none | machine-readable is the CRA/CISA baseline |
| **Embedded** | the SBOM lives **in** the image (OSF Firmware Embedded SBOM) vs. a sidecar | an embedded SBOM travels with the bytes; a sidecar can be lost |
| **Identity** | every component carries a GUID-form tag-id (== FILE_GUID) | the OSF identity MUST — anchors each module to a stable id |
| **Source-hash** | a source-file hash rides in `colloquial-version` | the OSF **M-srchash** MUST — ties the module to its source |
| **Byte-hash** | a shipped-byte / payload hash per component | the only thing that catches a **same-GUID byte swap** |
| **Signed** | a signed provenance/attestation accompanies the SBOM | evidence you can trust without re-running the toolchain |
| **Reconcile** | an operator can reconcile shipped bytes vs. the declared per-module hash | the check that actually blocks a re-signed trojan |

## What the real data says

- **Dell and Lenovo genuinely lead on the OSF embedding story.** Their firmware ships a real
  **embedded coSWID** (the uSWID `SBOM` container magic is present in the bytes), every component
  carries a **GUID tag-id**, and their code modules carry a **source-file hash in
  `colloquial-version`** — the OSF **M-srchash** MUST. Their microcode/CSME blobs do not (hence the
  ◐), which is honest: you can hash source you build, not an opaque blob.
- **This project leads on the two things nobody else does:** a **signed SLSA VSA** and an
  operator-side **shipped-byte reconcile**. Dell/Lenovo declare *what* a module is (id + source hash)
  but ship no per-module *shipped-byte* hash, so an operator cannot catch a same-GUID byte swap from
  their coSWID alone. That gap is exactly this project's thesis.
- **The honest gap in our own reference:** we score **⛔ on source-hash** — the edk2 source tree is
  not vendored here, so we emit no `edk2:sourceHash`. Dell/Lenovo beat us on that specific MUST. This
  is the same gap the gate reports as the advisory `osf-source-hash` control (see
  [`COMPLIANCE-MATRIX.md`](COMPLIANCE-MATRIX.md) §8) — the matrix and this comparison agree.
- **Most of the ecosystem ships nothing.** Prebuilt OVMF, coreboot, and Intel FSP/microcode carry no
  SBOM at all (score 0.0). This is not a knock on their engineering — coreboot's reproducible builds
  are excellent — it is the transparency-artifact gap the whole effort exists to close.

## The "best, cleanest" reference — a synthesis, not a single winner

No shipped provider is the model to copy wholesale. The **ideal** combines what each does well:

> **Dell/Lenovo's embedded coSWID + GUID identity + `colloquial-version` source hash**, carried
> **inside** the image (OSF embedding), **plus this project's per-module shipped-byte hash + signed
> SLSA VSA + operator-side reconcile.**

That composite is the target this repo's reference is built toward. It already has the byte-hash +
signed VSA + reconcile half; the concrete next step — **adopt a real `edk2:sourceHash`** so we meet
the M-srchash MUST the way Dell/Lenovo do — is tracked as the advisory `osf-source-hash` control and
the `--source-hashes` path in the emitter. Closing it would move our row to a clean lead on every
dimension.

## Reproducing / extending

```
make provider-comparison                    # prints the matrix from live probes
python3 scripts/provider-comparison.py --json    # machine-readable, per-dimension
```

Artifact locations are overridable so the harness runs anywhere (a missing artifact degrades to
UNKNOWN, never a fabricated pass):

| Env var | Default | Provider |
|---|---|---|
| `USWID_EXAMPLES` | `../python-uswid/examples` | Dell / Lenovo embedded coSWID |
| `OUR_SBOM` | `inputs/sbom.cdx.json` | this project's reference |
| `OVMF_PREBUILT` | `…/T71/…/OVMF_CODE_4M.fd` | Ubuntu OVMF prebuilt |
| `COREBOOT` | `…/T71/coreboot-blobs` | coreboot |
| `INTEL_FSP` | `…/T71/FSP` | Intel FSP / microcode |
| `USWID_BIN` | `../edk2-sbom/venv/bin/uswid` | the uswid decoder |

**Honesty caveats.** The Dell/Lenovo artifacts are Richard Hughes' *example* coSWID containers (a few
components each), not full production dumps — they are representative of the embedded-coSWID *shape*,
not a complete parts list. The prebuilt-OVMF / coreboot / Intel rows read real bytes on external
storage; when that storage is unmounted those rows report UNKNOWN, not a pass. "Signed" for Dell/Lenovo
is UNKNOWN here: LVFS signs its catalog (`.jcat`), which this per-image probe does not evaluate.
